scenario_stem:
A specialized apparel manufacturing business operates as a Private Limited Company, employing 45 full-time factory machinists and 5 supervisors across two workshop facilities. Operating for 7 years, the business generates $1.8m in annual revenue, with annual labor costs accounting for $650,000 of total operating expenses. Production relies heavily on a piece-rate payment system ($2.50 per completed denim jacket). However, worker demotivation and quality defects have increased as machinists rush garment assembly to maximize weekly earnings, causing a 28% annual staff turnover rate among workshop staff.

Morale among machinists has dropped due to repetitive stitching tasks and unpredictable weekly pay during slow demand periods. To improve staff retention and product quality, the HR director is deciding whether to replace piece rates with a fixed weekly salary combined with profit-sharing bonuses, or implement job enrichment by allowing machinists to inspect their own work and participate in new jacket design discussions.

questions.question_text: Define 'piece-rate payment'.
questions.model_answer: A payment system where workers are paid a fixed amount for each unit of output produced [2].

knowledge_max_2: payment system based on output produced

questions.model_answer: Problem 1: High recruitment and selection costs [k] to hire replacement factory machinists [app]. Problem 2: Lost production output [k] while new assembly workers complete basic machine training [app].

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits to this business of implementing job enrichment for its factory machinists.
questions.model_answer: Benefit 1: Higher job satisfaction and psychological fulfillment [k] as machinists participate in jacket design decisions [app], reducing absenteeism and staff turnover [an]. Benefit 2: Improved quality control awareness [k] as workers inspect their own garment assembly [app], reducing defect rates and lowering raw material waste [an].

analysis_max_2: reduces absenteeism/turnover
reduces defect rates/raw material waste

questions.question_text: Do you think introducing a fixed weekly salary with profit-sharing bonuses is a better motivation strategy for this business than implementing job enrichment? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: A fixed weekly salary provides income security for 45 machinists [k], removing financial pressure to rush jacket stitching [app] and lowering the 28% turnover rate [an]; profit-sharing further aligns worker effort with overall company profitability across both workshops. Conversely, job enrichment increases intrinsic motivation by giving machinists design input [k], but fails to address basic financial dissatisfaction caused by unpredictable piece-rate pay [app] when production slows down [an]. Overall, fixed salaries with profit-sharing are better because basic income security (Herzberg's hygiene factor) must be satisfied first to reduce 28% turnover [eval], whereas job enrichment alone will not satisfy workers if weekly earnings remain uncertain [eval].

scenario_stem:

scenario_stem:
A regional logistics and e-commerce fulfillment business operates as a Private Limited Company across 3 warehouse facilities, employing 95 parcel pickers and 3 shift supervisors. Operating for 10 years, the business generates $6.5m in annual revenue. The organizational structure features a very wide span of control, with each supervisor managing 32 pickers, alongside a tall hierarchy of 5 management tiers between warehouse staff and executive directors.

Operational efficiency has declined severely, with average order dispatch times increasing by 40%. Parcel pickers experience 6-hour delays when reporting barcode scanner failures or conveyor belt breakdowns because supervisors are overwhelmed with administrative tasks. Furthermore, an autocratic leadership style dominates, where senior managers issue rigid picking targets without consultation. Managing directors are evaluating whether to delayer the hierarchy by removing middle management tiers and delegating operational authority to team leaders, or transition to a democratic leadership style.

scenario_stem:
